newsitem.title: USA: Rexene says would not oppose $16/share cash bid.
newsitem.headline: Rexene says would not oppose $16/share cash bid.

text.p: Rexene Corp., which recently rejected a $490.7 million takeover bid by Huntsman Corp., said Thursday it would not oppose a fully-financed cash bid of $16 per share, but noted it has not received any offers that meet its conditions.
Huntsman's latest offer of $16 per share was rejected by Renexe in early December.

Dallas-based Rexene said the offer received from Huntsman "did not call for any financing and, in the view of the Rexene board, was highly conditional and not likely to lead to a transaction in the near term."

The maker of plastic film, which has rejected three unsolicited offers by Huntsman, is urging shareholders to reject a proposal by Wyser-Pratte & Co. Inc., its largest shareholder, to call a special meeting and install a new board.

Wyser-Pratte and Spear, Leeds & Kellogg, which together own about 10.1 percent of Rexene's outstanding common stock, are seeking the election of a majority of directors who would be committed to considering the bid by Huntsman as well as any higher offers by qualified purchasers.

Rexene said that even though an offer of $16 a share does not fully reflect the long-term prospects of the company, it would not oppose a fully-financed cash offer on customary terms at that price, "as long as the offer is capable of being consummated through a tender offer or otherwise within 60 days," Rexene Chairman Andrew Smith wrote in a letter to shareholders.
Rexene said it would take steps to invalidate its poison pill anti-takeover plan if it received an offer that met its conditions.

In opposing the Wyser-Pratte slate, Rexene said that Wyser-Pratte directors have no experience with the company and would be forced to manage it or sell it at a low price if a $16 per share deal did not materialise.
Rexene, through its Rexene Products and CT Film divisions, manufactures thermoplastic resins and plastic film through facilities in Texas, Wisconsin, Georgia, Delaware, Utah and in England.
Rexene's stock edged up 37.5 cents to $14 on the New York Stock Exchange.
